summary: This bill directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a three-year pilot program providing financial assistance to eligible individuals for purchasing medically necessary infant formula or donor milk through vouchers, reimbursements, or grants to local entities.

scores.thoughts: This bill establishes a pilot program to provide financial assistance for medically necessary infant formula and donor milk. This directly expands access to specific healthcare-related products for infants with medical needs or mothers unable to breastfeed, thus increasing public support for a component of healthcare.

The bill creates a new pilot program to provide financial assistance to eligible individuals for purchasing infant formula or donor milk, targeting those not eligible for WIC but still facing medical or other challenges. This expands a form of welfare or social support for specific families.

The bill authorizes $15 million per year in new appropriations for a 3-year pilot program with no offsets or revenue measures, increasing federal outlays and the deficit to fund this assistance priority.

The core of the bill is a new HHS pilot program that provides direct financial assistance (via vouchers, reimbursements, or grants) to purchase medically necessary infant formula or donor milk for eligible families, constituting government intervention to reduce out-of-pocket costs.
